title: Normalized point-sections comparison for the concrete Roos complex
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ with $k$ algebraically closed, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and put $R=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\Gamma$ for final-object sections with its canonical $\mathcal O_E$-action [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] [def-weil-point-section-scalar-functors], and $\Gamma^\bullet$ for its termwise functor on cochain complexes. Let $Q_{\mathcal O_E}$ be localization of ordinary $\mathcal O_E$-module complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the same coefficient-size lift as the point fibre [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a strict tower $T$ of complexes in an abelian category with countable products, use $H(T)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_T)[-1]$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], with $1-s_T$ the transition endomorphism of the product [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], whose degree $i$ has coordinates $(b,a)\in\prod_nT_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nT_n^i$. Define $\operatorname{roosFirst}(T,n,i)$ to be the unshifted projection $(b,a)\mapsto a_n$, and $\operatorname{roosSecond}(T,n,i)$ to be the shifted projection $(b,a)\mapsto b_n$. For each strict tower $T$ of $R$-module complexes on $s$, define $c_T:\Gamma^\bullet H(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T\mathbin{;}\Gamma^\bullet)$ to be the unique chain isomorphism satisfying, for every $n,i$,
$$\operatorname{roosFirst}(T\mathbin{;}\Gamma^\bullet,n,i)\circ c_T^i=\Gamma(\operatorname{roosFirst}(T,n,i)),\qquad
\operatorname{roosSecond}(T\mathbin{;}\Gamma^\bullet,n,i)\circ c_T^i=\Gamma(\operatorname{roosSecond}(T,n,i)).$$
Here existence and uniqueness are the product-and-biproduct comparison: sections preserve products, the additive functor preserves the signed cone differential, the inverse is given by the inverse product identifications, and both sets of projections jointly determine each degree map. The Lean declarations are respectively sectionsComplex, moduleQ, roosFirst, roosSecond, sectionsRoos_existsUnique and sectionsRoos; the last chooses the uniquely normalized comparison, without invoking any reparametrization-coherence theorem.
